editorial:
If you have ever been blindsided by a breakup and spent weeks replaying every little moment, this movie will hit you right in the chest. Tom is a hopeless romantic who writes greeting cards for a living, and when Summer walks into his life, he is convinced she is the one. The catch is that Summer does not believe in true love, and Tom refuses to see the warning signs. Told out of order, the story jumps between happy days and painful ones, so you feel the same confusion and heartbreak Tom does. It is funny, sad, and painfully relatable all at once.

The acting is fantastic, especially the way the leads capture that awkward, giddy energy of a new crush and the slow fade that follows. The soundtrack is great, the pacing keeps you engaged, and the split-screen expectations versus reality scene is unforgettable. On the downside, Tom can be frustratingly stubborn, and some viewers may find the nonlinear structure a bit jarring at first. Still, if you enjoy smart romantic comedies with real emotional weight, this one is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: After months of heartbreak, Tom finally accepts that Summer was never going to be his forever person. He quits his greeting card job and pursues his dream of becoming an architect. In the final scene, he goes to a job interview and meets a new woman named Autumn. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting Tom has learned from his past and is ready to try again, this time with someone who might actually share his romantic outlook.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart romantic comedies with real emotional depth.
